html:
The contractor says the job is finished, the painters have packed up, and your Greer kitchen still looks like someone dusted it with flour. That fine gray film is drywall dust, and it is why post construction cleaning in Greer SC exists as its own service. If this is your first time hiring one, here are the questions homeowners ask us most, answered in the order they usually come up.

What is post-construction cleaning, and how is it different from a regular clean?

A regular visit maintains a home that is already clean. Post-construction cleaning removes what a building project leaves behind. The team handles fine construction dust on surfaces, ledges and trim, the inside of cabinets, drawers and closets, windows, glass, tracks and sills, paint specks, sticker residue and adhesive, light fixtures, vents and ceiling fans, bathrooms and new fixtures, and floors that are vacuumed and washed in multiple passes. The last step is a touch-up pass before you move in or start using the room.

Drywall sanding makes the finest dust, and it travels. After a remodel it lands inside closed cabinets and on top of door frames, which is why a quick wipe leaves it behind. Our post construction cleaning in Greer is built around getting that dust out of places a household cloth never reaches.

A typical sign you need it: you wipe a counter, and the cloth comes away gray. Another is a sticker still on a new window, or a line of paint along a glass edge that no household spray lifts. These details are slow, careful work, and they are the difference between a house that looks finished and one that only looks built.

Who usually books it in Greer?

Most calls come from four groups: homeowners finishing a remodel or addition, builders and general contractors who want a clean handoff, buyers closing on new construction, and families with a kitchen or bathroom renovation. Greer is where we are based, and the jobs range from updates in historic homes near Downtown Greer and Trade Street to new construction near GSP Airport and the BMW plant. Roads like I-85, SC-14, SC-101 and US-29 put most of these jobs within a short drive of our team.

What should I do before the cleaners arrive?

  • Ask the contractor to remove debris, scrap material and tools first. We clean, we do not haul.
  • Finish the punch list if you can. Cleaning before the last touch-up means dust returns.
  • Keep power and water on, since fixtures and appliances are cleaned and checked.
  • Cover or move anything you do not want in the work area.
  • Mention special surfaces, such as new stone or unsealed floors, so the team uses the right method.

It also helps to tell us how many phases you want. A rough clean after the messy work, a final clean after the trades leave and a touch-up can be booked together, and many first-timers choose that route.

How much does post construction cleaning cost in Greer?

We do not post a price, and we never quote one over the phone. Perfect Services gives an exact price only after a free in-home estimate, a short visit to see the space with no commitment. What shapes it is straightforward: the project size in square feet and rooms affected, the dust level, how many phases you book, how much glass and residue there is, and any deadline from a closing or inspection that might call for a larger team. To book the visit, use the form on the city page, call (864) 399-5168 or text (864) 666-8520.

What does the first visit look like?

The estimator walks the same path the cleaners will: kitchen and bathrooms first, then windows, then floors and trim. They check how much sanding dust there is, whether paint or adhesive has dried on glass, and what finish the floors have. Then they explain what is included and give the price. You can ask to have the clean scheduled close to your inspection or move-in date, and if the dates are firm, say so at the start so the right crew size is planned.

If you want to see how one common problem is handled, our article on removing paint, stickers and residue after construction in Greer goes into detail. Neighbors in Taylors can find the same service at post-construction cleaning in Taylors.

One more thing first-timers ask: do you need to be home? Not for the clean itself, but we do like to meet you at the start to hear which rooms matter most, and again at the end for the walkthrough. If a builder is handing off the home to a buyer, the contractor can be the contact instead.

What should I expect afterwards?

Walk through with the crew lead if you can, with a flashlight held at an angle across counters and windows. That light shows what a normal look misses. The first week after, you may still see a little dust settle from the air handling system, particularly if the HVAC ran during the work. That is normal and worth mentioning to your contractor. Many homeowners also book deep cleaning a few weeks later to reset the home after the move-in. The full overview of the service sits on our post-construction cleaning page, and you can start from the free estimate form on the home page.

faqs: Does post-construction cleaning include hauling debris?
No. The contractor should remove scrap and trash first. The team cleans surfaces, glass, fixtures and floors after that.
Can I book rough and final cleans together?
Yes. The rough clean, final clean and touch-up can be booked together, which many first-time customers in Greer prefer.
Is a post-construction clean needed after a small bathroom remodel?
Usually yes. Even a small remodel creates fine dust that settles in vents, trim and drawers, and the estimate visit will show how much work remains.
